tasks.title: Correct authoritative clock precision and care contracts
tasks.spec: Implement a fresh forward-only public-contract correction from the exact accepted FOUND-BASELOCK-001 SHA without merging or cherry-picking CONTRACT-CORR-001, CONTRACT-CORR-002, CONTRACT-CORR-003, or any rejected Attempt. Reimplement the complete exact comparator, care timing, bounded resolution, audits, examples, and documentation required by CONTRACT-CORR-003. Preserve TimestampSchema's full offset-aware arbitrary-fraction domain. Export one dependency-free package-root compareTimestamps function that uses exact integer calendar and offset arithmetic plus digit-wise fractional comparison without Date.parse, epoch milliseconds, rounding, truncation, fixed precision, large exponentiation, or a new dependency. Keep the existing general-purpose Clock.now Date contract source-compatible for accepted non-care modules. Add a package-root CareClock whose now method returns a Timestamp that adapters must validate with TimestampSchema, so care commands can retain the authoritative instant verbatim without toISOString or any Date conversion. Set the care command time policy source to CareClock.now and document the validation precondition and precision guarantee. Use the same comparator for AcknowledgedCareEventSchema and TimeRangeSchema. Preserve strict now-before-deadline semantics, caller-timestamp rejection, the explicit escalated late-acknowledgement path, bounded persisted care resolution, migration-only legacy_unknown visibility, closure preservation, and content-free resolution audits.
acceptance: The task starts from the exact accepted FOUND-BASELOCK-001 SHA and no rejected Attempt SHA is an ancestor
The public package exports one documented compareTimestamps function returning -1, 0, or 1 for any two values accepted by TimestampSchema
The existing general-purpose Clock.now Date signature remains source-compatible, while package-root CareClock.now returns a TimestampSchema-validated precision-preserving value
No CareClock or care timing path uses Date, Date.parse, toISOString, epoch milliseconds, fixed precision, rounding, truncation, or a new dependency
A CareClock fixture at 2026-08-27T20:01:00.000998Z is timely before a 2026-08-27T20:01:00.000999Z deadline, while exact equality and any later instant are not timely
Equivalent instants with different offsets, omitted optional seconds, or trailing fractional zeros compare equal
Microsecond, beyond-nanosecond, cross-day offset, leap-day, year-0000, and long-fraction fixtures compare exactly and preserve antisymmetry and transitivity
TimeRangeSchema accepts genuinely positive sub-millisecond and beyond-nanosecond ranges and rejects canonically equal endpoints
Strict request schemas reject acknowledgedAt and handledAt supplied by callers
Handled events require one bounded resolution, closed events preserve it, and legacy_unknown remains history-only
The escalated-to-acknowledged late path remains valid and is never classified as timely
Resolution audits remain bounded and content-free, and every public operation and schema example validates
TimestampSchema is not narrowed and no lockfile, unrelated API, privacy, handover, or UI contract changes

update_tasks.spec: Implement a fresh responsibility capability from the exact accepted CONTRACT-CORR-004 SHA without merging or cherry-picking RESP-001, RESP-REPAIR-001, RESP-REPAIR-002, or any rejected Attempt. Before provider invocation, validate the active requesting actor and every exact selected signal, provenance, evidence, and source member; identities must agree and every source member must be active in the same space with analysisConsent enabled. Build the entire provider request only from server-owned allowlisted metadata and bounded redacted excerpts. Never forward an arbitrary caller promptVersion or any raw or private content, raw reference, or persistent entity identifier in any provider-bound field; validate the whole provider request and compare UUID forms case-insensitively. Synchronous throws, asynchronous rejection, timeout, and two invalid outputs must return bounded review with zero consequential mutation. Revalidate the guard after provider return. Issue only an opaque server-side integrity-bound draft receipt. Confirmation must atomically resolve idempotency, verify the same authorized actor and immutable server-side draft plus current guard, consume the receipt, and persist once; an exact replay after consumption returns the original domain, while a different actor, key, payload, or tampered draft fails without mutation. Resolve correction idempotency before mutable-state and no-op validation, generate audit identity and time only on a replay miss, and return the original content-free audit on replay. Import the CONTRACT-CORR-004 package-root exact timestamp comparator for report-period boundaries. Derive reports deterministically from the five persisted stages, separate hidden coordination from execution, exclude ineligible facts, and use frozen neutral Chinese templates without an LLM.
acceptance: The task starts from the exact accepted CONTRACT-CORR-004 SHA and no rejected Attempt SHA is an ancestor
Unauthorized actor, space, task, signal, evidence, source member, or non-exact selected set fails before provider invocation
Revoked, inactive, missing, cross-space, or identity-mismatched source members leave provider and mutation counts at zero
Every provider-bound field uses server-owned allowlisted metadata and contains no raw content, raw reference, or persistent entity identifier
A caller promptVersion containing a selected UUID or private text is rejected before the provider, and uppercase UUID variants cannot bypass the provider-payload guard
Synchronous provider throw, asynchronous rejection, timeout, and invalid first and second outputs return bounded review with zero attribution, report, or domain mutation
Actor or source consent, membership, visibility, evidence, review, or version drift during provider execution produces zero mutation
Fabricated, failed-call, wrong-actor, field-tampered, or wrong-idempotency confirmations cannot persist
An exact opaque-receipt confirmation replay after receipt consumption returns the original domain with one total mutation; same receipt with different authority or payload conflicts
Exact correction replay returns the original task and audit ID and time with one total mutation; same-key different payload conflicts and stale new requests write nothing
Corrections require an authorized actor and expected version, and audit metadata remains content-free
Report period boundaries import compareTimestamps from the package root and preserve positive microsecond ranges plus equivalent-offset equality without Date parsing or local timestamp logic
Every report cell traces to the five persisted responsibility fields and authorized current signals; discussion-only, evidence_missing, and needs_review facts are excluded
A four-hidden-stages-to-one-member and execution-to-another fixture uses exactly 本周家庭协调工作集中在一位成员身上。虽然执行任务有所分担，但发现、安排与跟进仍未形成完整责任所有权。
Empty, balanced, and uneven fixtures remain deterministic and contain no score, rank, blame, diagnosis, or relationship judgment

update_tasks.spec: Implement a fresh care capability against CONTRACT-CORR-004 and DATA-CORR-001 without merging any rejected attempt. Import the package-root exact timestamp comparator and CareClock, and use them for every acknowledgement-deadline decision. Validate CareClock.now as a precision-preserving Timestamp, read it once per command, and reuse that exact value for deadline decisions, transition timestamps, idempotency persistence, domain events, and audits; Date, Date.parse, toISOString, epoch-millisecond comparison, precision narrowing, and duplicate local timestamp parsers are forbidden in the care path. Acknowledgement is timely only when server now is strictly before the acknowledgement deadline; equality or lateness cannot suppress escalation. Persist and audit the bounded handling resolution and retain it through closure. Enforce one PostgreSQL lock order: care events in deterministic ID order before care rules in deterministic ID order. Add a credential-free disposable PostgreSQL race test using existing locked dependencies and a care-local harness.
acceptance: Caller-controlled timestamps cannot backdate acknowledgement or handling
An unconfirmed draft rule cannot schedule, notify, acknowledge, or escalate
Only the subject actor can acknowledge and only the current escalation recipient can handle
Wrong-space, inactive, or unrelated actors fail closed without any event, rule, notification, idempotency, or audit mutation
CareClock.now is validated once as Timestamp and its exact fractional precision is reused without Date conversion
Acknowledgement succeeds only when CareClock.now is strictly before the deadline, including a one-microsecond positive margin
Equivalent instants expressed with different offsets and the exact deadline cannot suppress timeout or escalation
The existing escalated-to-acknowledged late path remains valid and is never classified as a timely acknowledgement
The implementation imports the contract comparator and contains no Date, Date.parse, toISOString, epoch-millisecond deadline comparison, or duplicate timestamp parser
Handling requires the current escalation recipient and persists and audits the bounded resolution
Closure preserves the handling resolution
Concurrent scheduler and acknowledgement transactions complete without deadlock, duplicate event, or contradictory terminal result
Repeated ticks, acknowledgements, and handling requests are idempotent
No path uses an LLM, wall-clock sleep, Date.now, or free-form care resolution
